acceptanceCriteria.criterion: All destructive database operations (DELETE, TRUNCATE, drop_collection) check APP_ENV before execution - Unit test verifies operations fail in production without explicit override
Production operations require explicit --force-production flag or interactive confirmation - Integration test validates confirmation prompt appears
Clear logging indicates which environment (PRODUCTION/TEST) is being modified - Log output inspection in unit tests
Scripts that modify databases display prominent warning banner for production - Manual verification of script output
ingest_pdf() requires explicit clear_existing=True parameter to delete existing data - Unit test validates default behavior preserves data
New SafetyGuard utility class centralizes all protection logic - Code review verifies single source of truth

constraints.constraint: SafetyGuard MUST be ~80 lines max. No abstract base classes, no custom decorators, no configuration frameworks. Simple utility class only.
Only use libraries listed in docs/architecture/5-technology-stack-definitive.md. No new dependencies allowed without user approval.
Reuse existing Settings.app_env field - do NOT duplicate environment detection logic. SafetyGuard.is_production should check settings.app_env == 'production' AND settings.qdrant_port == 6333.
SafetyGuard checks are O(1) string comparisons. Zero performance impact on normal operations.
Existing scripts work unchanged - default safe behavior means no breaking changes for scripts that don't explicitly clear data.
Project target is ~600-800 lines. SafetyGuard adds ~80 lines - ensure it stays minimal.

tests.standards: Unit tests in tests/unit/ with no external dependencies. Use monkeypatch to set APP_ENV environment variable. Mock sys.stdin.isatty() to test interactive/non-interactive modes. Integration tests use test database infrastructure from Story 4.0.5 (Qdrant:6335, PostgreSQL:5433). Target 80%+ coverage on new code. Follow pytest-asyncio patterns for async functions.
